questions.stem: Under UNCLOS (1982), a coastal state's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends from its shore baseline to a maximum of:

options.option_text: 12 nautical miles (the territorial-sea limit)
200 nautical miles (about 370 km from the baseline)
350 nautical miles (only continental-shelf claim)
500 nautical miles (no such limit in UNCLOS)

questions.explanation: UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982) — defines maritime zones. Territorial sea: 12 nm (full sovereignty). Contiguous zone: 24 nm (limited control). EEZ: 200 nm (sovereign rights over economic resources — fishing, oil, gas, mining). Continental shelf: 200 nm or further if naturally extending (max 350 nm). India's EEZ ~ 2.3 million km² — among the world's largest. Distractor 1 = territorial sea. Distractor 3 = extended shelf claim cap. Distractor 4 = invented.

questions.stem: POLYMETALLIC NODULES on the deep-ocean floor are commercially valuable mainly for their content of:

options.option_text: Gold, silver, platinum traces only
Manganese, nickel, copper, cobalt
Lithium, sodium, potassium salts
Uranium and rare-earth elements only

questions.explanation: Polymetallic / manganese nodules — potato-sized rocks scattered on abyssal plains (~4-6 km depth). Composition: ~30% manganese, 1.3% nickel, 1.1% copper, 0.2% cobalt, plus iron + traces. Critical for batteries (Ni, Co), stainless steel (Mn), electronics. India has been allotted a 75,000 km² PMN exploration site in the Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB) by the International Seabed Authority — first developing country to get such allotment (1987). Deep-sea mining is technically feasible but environmentally controversial — ISA has not yet finalised commercial-extraction rules.

questions.stem: India's MAJOR offshore oil and gas field, accounting for ~40% of domestic production, is the:

options.option_text: Krishna-Godavari basin off Andhra coast
Bombay High in the Arabian Sea, off Mumbai
Cambay basin off Gujarat's western coast
Andaman offshore basin near Port Blair

questions.explanation: Bombay High — discovered 1974 by ONGC, ~160 km off Mumbai. Production began 1976. Single largest oil + gas field in India; offshore platform 'Sagar Samrat' was the rig. Krishna-Godavari (KG) basin (off AP coast) — major gas field; Reliance KG-D6 block. Cambay basin — onshore + shallow offshore Gujarat (small fields). Andaman basin — under exploration; potential not yet large. India imports ~85% of crude needs despite Bombay High; demand far exceeds domestic output.

questions.stem: The world's most productive marine fishing grounds typically occur where:

options.option_text: Two warm ocean currents converge over deep water
Cold and warm currents meet over a continental shelf
An equatorial current flows steadily eastward
Coral reefs form along tropical island shores

questions.explanation: Major fishing grounds — Grand Banks (Canada, Labrador-Gulf Stream meeting), Doggerbank (North Sea), Hokkaido (Oyashio-Kuroshio), Peruvian coast (Humboldt upwelling). Cold + warm currents meet → strong upwelling brings nutrient-rich deep water to the surface → plankton bloom → fish abundance. Continental shelves (< 200 m depth) provide ideal habitat. Distractor 1 — convergence of two warm currents creates a stratified, low-nutrient zone. Distractor 3 — equatorial currents are too uniform thermally. Distractor 4 — coral reefs are biodiverse but small in total fish biomass compared to temperate shelves.

questions.stem: The 'BLUE REVOLUTION' in the Indian context refers to:

options.option_text: Rapid expansion of inland water transport corridors
Rapid expansion of fish production from rivers and seas
Drinking-water coverage to every rural household
Cleaning the Ganga under the Namami Gange mission

questions.explanation: Blue Revolution — initiated under the Fish Farmers Development Agency (1973-74) and accelerated under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY, 2020). Aim: boost India's fish production. India is now the SECOND largest fish producer in the world (after China). FY24 production ~17 million tonnes. Major contributors: Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Gujarat. Other 'colour' revolutions: Green (foodgrain), White (milk — Operation Flood, Verghese Kurien), Yellow (oilseeds), Pink (onions/meat), Silver (eggs), Golden (fruits/horticulture).

questions.stem: The MARIANA TRENCH, the deepest known point in any ocean, is located in the:

options.option_text: South Atlantic Ocean near Antarctica
Western Pacific Ocean east of the Philippines
North Indian Ocean near Sri Lanka
Arctic Ocean near the North Pole region

questions.explanation: Mariana Trench — Western Pacific, east of the Mariana Islands, just east of the Philippines. Depth ~10,994 m at the Challenger Deep — deepest known point on Earth. Formed by the Pacific Plate subducting under the smaller Mariana Plate. First crewed descent — 1960 (Trieste — Jacques Piccard, Don Walsh). Second — 2012 (James Cameron solo dive). Other deep trenches: Tonga (~10,800 m), Philippine (~10,500 m), Java/Sunda (~7,400 m, deepest in Indian Ocean), Puerto Rico (~8,400 m, deepest in Atlantic).

questions.stem: The 'GARBAGE PATCH' in the North Pacific is primarily made up of:

options.option_text: Floating logs from large-scale rainforest deforestation
Tiny plastic fragments accumulated by ocean gyre currents
Toxic chemical sludge from offshore oil-rig leaks
Sunken cargo from container-ship spills near Hawaii

questions.explanation: Great Pacific Garbage Patch — between Hawaii and California; ~1.6 million km² (~3× the size of France). Composed mostly of MICROPLASTICS (1-5 mm fragments) plus larger plastic debris, fishing nets, bottles. Concentrated by the North Pacific subtropical gyre — converging currents trap floating debris. The water is not solid garbage as often imagined; it's a 'plastic soup' with high concentrations. Five major ocean gyres globally — each has a similar garbage patch (Indian Ocean, North Atlantic, South Pacific, South Atlantic). Plastic enters the food chain via marine animals; ~80% of marine plastic comes from land-based sources, primarily rivers in developing countries.
